exposure: Women who did not re-present with hypertension
Peak systolic blood pressure during delivery admission
Women who re-presented to hospital with hypertension within 28 days postpartum
cohort: 17,746 women who delivered at a tertiary metropolitan hospital in Melbourne, Australia from 1 January 2016 to 30 December 2020
finding: A risk model using six factors (pre-eclampsia, gestational hypertension, peak systolic blood pressure in the delivery admission, aspirin prescription, and elective caesarean delivery) showed good discriminative ability (C-statistic of 0.90) for predicting postpartum hypertension re-presentation within 28 days.
mod_finding: Elective caesarean delivery was a significant predictor of postpartum hypertension re-presentation.
